title: Networking
subtitle: A request is a stack of round trips, and each one costs time
keyInsight: Most page load time is round trips, not bandwidth, so each protocol generation wins by needing fewer of them.

decisions.title: Model time in round trips
decisions.description: The sim counts round trips and multiplies by the round-trip time, so the effect of each protocol change is visible without modeling bandwidth.
decisions.alternatives: A byte-level bandwidth model is closer to a real browser but buries the one idea, that handshakes dominate small requests.

decisions.title: Show the worst case beside the average
decisions.description: The HTTP/3 frame reports the users whose network blocks UDP, so learners see that a faster protocol can have a slower tail.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting only the happy path would make HTTP/3 look strictly better and hide the fallback cost.
